newsitem.title: UK: MultiMedia sees 1996 loss on weak CD-ROMs.
newsitem.headline: MultiMedia sees 1996 loss on weak CD-ROMs.

text.p: CD-ROM publisher MultiMedia Corp Plc on Friday said it expects to post a pre-tax loss for the 1996 year of 750,000 to one million stg, reflecting difficulties in the CD-ROM market and a writedown in the carrying value of its investments in CD-ROM titles.

MultiMedia, like other CD-ROM publishers, has been plagued by market weakness, particularly in North America where CD-ROMs have failed to take off as expected. The U.S. represents about one-third of the CD-ROM market, but customers there are focusing more on downloading information from the Internet rather than buying CD-ROMs.
MultiMedia said its problems in the CD-ROM market, particularly in North America, continued in the second half of 1996.

"Not only have advances for some titles been significantly lower than we hoped, but we have also experienced delays in commissioning of titles which has led to us having periodic over-capacity," chairman Duncan Thomas said in a statement.
The recent strength of sterling has also reduced the value of the company's substantial export income, Thomas said.
Dorling Kindersley Holdings Plc, another British-based publisher of CD-ROMs, in December said the strength of sterling would squeeze its 1996 profits.
MultiMedia's media database business, Content Management Corp, suffered from a long sales cycle and sales which it had hoped to achieve in 1996 have been delayed to 1997, Thomas said.

Failure to reach an agreement with Ford Motor Co on the commission to enhance the sytem for Ford's use over the Internet also hurt business. The Ford contract would have had a value of about 120,000 stg, Thomas said.

"Current business remains difficult, but there have also been positive developments," Thomas said. "We have secured the rights to develop two high-profile titles with strong branding which we hope and expect to be as attractive to publishers as 'Sophie's World.' "

MultiMedia has not yet received reports from publishers on Christmas sales of some new titles, but information received to date has been positive, with the Oxford Children's Encyclopedia and Mensa having positive launches, Thomas said.
The company has taken steps to reduce its overheads by about 500,000 pounds a year, Thomas said.

MultiMedia, meanwhile, is exploring opportunties in the emerging Digital Versatile Disk market and is focusing its marketing increasingly on business-to-business work, particularly in the intranet publishing field.
